```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(dsprrr)

old_cache <- configure_cache(enable = FALSE)

```

`flex()` makes the program structure part of the optimization target. GEPA can
change the number or order of predictor calls and, in executable mode, add
deterministic logic or call a tool supplied by your application. Flex is
experimental, so its source format and behavior may change.

Start with declarative JSON when the workflow is a bounded graph of model
steps. Use executable R only when the task calls for branching, computation,
predictors created at run time, or named tools.

| What may change? | Use | Execution boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Instructions or examples inside a fixed module | A regular module and teleprompter | Normal module runtime |
| A known sequence of model steps | JSON Flex | Validated data; no code interpreter |
| Branches, deterministic logic, or selected tools | Executable Flex | Fresh runner; sandbox optimizer-authored code |

## A small JSON run needs no interpreter

The default source is a one-step JSON program. This example runs a real
`run()` call against a deterministic local Chat fixture. It needs neither an
API key nor a separate code interpreter:

```{r task-signature}
library(dsprrr)

route_signature <- signature(
  "ticket -> queue: enum('database', 'security', 'payments', 'identity')",
  instructions = "Route each support ticket to its owning queue."
)
```

Before running the JSON example in your own R session, run the fixture
definitions in the [appendix](#appendix-offline-fixture-source) once. The
deterministic Chat fixture counts actual task and proposer requests, while its
fixed response rules leave metric scoring and candidate selection to GEPA.

```{r offline-fixture, include=FALSE}
fixture_chat_class <- R6::R6Class(
  "Chat",
  public = list(
    turns = NULL,
    initialize = function(model, responder) {
      self$turns <- list()
      private$model <- ellmer::Model(name = model, extra_args = list())
      private$provider <- ellmer::Provider(name = "fixture", base_url = "")
      private$responder <- responder
    },
    chat = function(prompt, ...) {
      private$responder(paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n"), NULL, ...)
    },
    chat_structured = function(prompt, type, ...) {
      private$responder(
        paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n"),
        type,
        ...
      )
    },
    stream = function(...) character(),
    get_turns = function() self$turns,
    set_turns = function(turns) {
      self$turns <- turns
      invisible(self)
    },
    last_turn = function(role = NULL) NULL,
    get_model = function() private$model@name,
    get_provider = function() private$provider,
    get_model_object = function() private$model
  ),
  private = list(model = NULL, provider = NULL, responder = NULL),
  lock_objects = FALSE,
  parent_env = globalenv()
)

new_route_fixture <- function(
  proposed_source = NULL,
  model = "fixture-router"
) {
  audit <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  audit$prompts <- character()
  audit$proposal_calls <- 0L
  audit$task_calls <- 0L

  responder <- function(prompt, type, ...) {
    prompt <- paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n")
    audit$prompts <- c(audit$prompts, prompt)
    fields <- names(type@properties)

    if (identical(fields, "module_src")) {
      if (is.null(proposed_source)) {
        stop("The JSON example does not configure a proposer")
      }
      audit$proposal_calls <- audit$proposal_calls + 1L
      return(list(module_src = proposed_source))
    }

    if (!identical(fields, "queue")) {
      stop("Unexpected structured output requested by the fixture")
    }
    audit$task_calls <- audit$task_calls + 1L

    queue <- if (
      grepl(
        "INC-DB-17|Queries time out|Read traffic",
        prompt,
        ignore.case = TRUE
      )
    ) {
      "database"
    } else if (
      grepl(
        "INC-SEC-9|unusual-login|login spray",
        prompt,
        ignore.case = TRUE
      )
    ) {
      "security"
    } else if (
      grepl(
        "INC-PAY-4|renewal|duplicate charge|Card charged twice",
        prompt,
        ignore.case = TRUE
      )
    ) {
      "payments"
    } else if (
      grepl("Password reset|Reset email", prompt, ignore.case = TRUE)
    ) {
      "identity"
    } else {
      stop("Unexpected ticket in the deterministic task fixture")
    }

    list(queue = queue)
  }

  list(
    chat = fixture_chat_class$new(model, responder),
    audit = audit
  )
}
```

```{r json-example}
json_program <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(flex(route_signature)))
json_fixture <- new_route_fixture()

json_result <- run(
  json_program,
  ticket = "[INC-SEC-9] unusual-login burst",
  .llm = json_fixture$chat,
  .cache = FALSE,
  .return_format = "structured"
)

cat(json_program$module_src, "\n")
json_result$output
json_result$metadata$predictor_calls
stopifnot(
  identical(json_result$output, list(queue = "security")),
  identical(json_result$metadata$predictor_calls, 1L)
)
```

The fixture makes task predictions repeatable. The router below still runs
through Flex's actual R bridge, predictor, tool, `compile()` and `evaluate()`
contracts. The fixed proposer demonstrates the optimizer plumbing; a live
search is needed to assess whether a model can discover this candidate.

## The routing task

A support team routes tickets to database, security, payments, or identity.
Some tickets have an incident code with a catalog owner. Others need a
language-model prediction. The search uses separate training and validation
rows. The holdout data is introduced only after compilation.

```{r router-data}
train <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "[INC-SEC-9] unusual-login burst",
    "Password reset links expire immediately"
  ),
  queue = c("security", "identity")
)

validation <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "[INC-PAY-4] capture queue is growing",
    "Renewal created two invoices"
  ),
  queue = c("payments", "payments")
)

stopifnot(length(intersect(train$ticket, validation$ticket)) == 0L)
```

The named catalog is application-owned. Executable Flex can request only this
tool; the optimizer does not receive the closure environment or the rest of
the R session.

```{r router-tool}
lookup_incident <- local({
  catalog <- c(
    "INC-DB-17" = "database",
    "INC-SEC-9" = "security",
    "INC-PAY-4" = "payments"
  )

  function(ticket) {
    hit <- names(catalog)[vapply(
      names(catalog),
      grepl,
      logical(1),
      x = ticket,
      fixed = TRUE
    )]
    if (!length(hit)) {
      return(list(found = FALSE))
    }
    list(found = TRUE, queue = unname(catalog[[hit[[1L]]]]))
  }
})

lookup_incident("[INC-DB-17] replicas unavailable")
lookup_incident("A password reset email is late")
```

## Compile with a deterministic proposer

This executable R example needs `callr`, an optional dsprrr dependency used
by `r_code_runner()` to start an R subprocess. Install it once before
continuing:

```{r install-callr, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("callr")
```

The baseline makes one predictor call for every ticket. The fixed, reviewed
candidate first asks the catalog about incident codes, returns a known owner
directly, and calls one predictor for everything else.

The following Chat fixture returns that candidate when GEPA asks for
`module_src`. For task predictions it returns a deterministic response from
the prompt's ticket text. GEPA runs the metric on Flex predictions and traces,
then selects from the resulting validation scores.

```{r router-sources}
baseline_source <- paste(
  "router <- Predict(\"$outer\", instructions = \"Choose the owning queue.\")",
  "forward <- function(ticket) router(ticket = ticket)",
  sep = "\n"
)

selected_fixture_source <- paste(
  "fallback <- Predict(\"$outer\", instructions = \"Route tickets without a known incident code.\")",
  "forward <- function(ticket) {",
  "  if (grepl(\"INC-\", ticket, fixed = TRUE)) {",
  "    hit <- lookup_incident(ticket = ticket)",
  "    if (isTRUE(hit$found)) return(Prediction(queue = hit$queue))",
  "  }",
  "  fallback(ticket = ticket)",
  "}",
  sep = "\n"
)

make_router <- function(module_src) {
  suppressWarnings(flex(
    route_signature,
    module_src = module_src,
    tools = list(lookup_incident = lookup_incident),
    interpreter_factory = r_code_runner,
    source_format = "r",
    require_sandbox = FALSE,
    max_predictor_calls = 1L,
    max_tool_calls = 1L
  ))
}

baseline <- make_router(baseline_source)
```

This offline article runs only the two fixed source strings shown here through
`r_code_runner()`. That runner starts an R subprocess, but it is not a security
sandbox. `require_sandbox = FALSE` is appropriate here only because both
sources are reviewed fixtures. For optimizer-authored R in an application,
keep the default sandbox requirement and configure an enforced runner such as
`mcp_repl_runner()` with [Posit's MCP Console][mcp-console].

[mcp-console]: https://github.com/posit-dev/mcp-console

The metric checks the predicted queue against the row label. Correct answers
score higher when they require no predictor; incorrect answers score zero.
The execution trace supplies the call count used for that efficiency reward.

```{r router-metric}
route_metric <- metric_with_trace(
  function(prediction, expected, program_trace) {
    correct <- identical(
      as.character(prediction$queue),
      as.character(expected$queue[[1L]])
    )
    predictor_calls <- program_trace$metadata$predictor_calls
    if (is.null(predictor_calls)) {
      predictor_calls <- 0L
    }

    list(
      score = if (!correct) {
        0
      } else if (predictor_calls == 0L) {
        1
      } else {
        0.5
      },
      feedback = if (!correct) {
        sprintf(
          "Expected '%s'; got '%s'.",
          expected$queue[[1L]],
          prediction$queue
        )
      } else if (predictor_calls > 0L) {
        "Correct route; prefer the incident catalog when it has an owner."
      } else {
        "Correct route without a predictor call."
      }
    )
  },
  field = "queue"
)
```

GEPA's validation score ranks the candidates. The `evaluate()` calls made by
`compile()` execute the bound Flex program, and `route_metric` reads the
resulting prediction and trace. Training rows are available to generate
feedback; validation rows decide which candidate survives.

```{r router-compile}
optimizer_fixture <- new_route_fixture(
  proposed_source = selected_fixture_source,
  model = "fixture-gepa-router"
)

optimized <- compile(
  baseline,
  GEPA(
    metric = route_metric,
    population_size = 2L,
    generations = 1L,
    selection = "current_best",
    track_best_outputs = TRUE,
    verbose = FALSE
  ),
  trainset = train,
  valset = validation,
  .llm = optimizer_fixture$chat,
  control = optimizer_control(
    max_metric_calls = 40L,
    max_provider_calls = 30L,
    max_elapsed_seconds = 300,
    num_threads = 1L,
    progress = FALSE
  )
)

compile_result <- optimization_result(optimized)
gepa_budget <- compile_result$budget

budget_summary <- data.frame(
  status = compile_result$status,
  metric_calls = gepa_budget$metric_calls,
  metric_call_limit = gepa_budget$limits$max_metric_calls,
  provider_calls = gepa_budget$provider_calls,
  provider_call_limit = gepa_budget$limits$max_provider_calls,
  task_calls = optimizer_fixture$audit$task_calls,
  proposal_calls = optimizer_fixture$audit$proposal_calls
)

stopifnot(
  identical(compile_result$status, "completed"),
  isTRUE(gepa_budget$metric_calls <= gepa_budget$limits$max_metric_calls),
  isTRUE(gepa_budget$provider_calls <= gepa_budget$limits$max_provider_calls),
  identical(
    gepa_budget$provider_calls,
    optimizer_fixture$audit$task_calls + optimizer_fixture$audit$proposal_calls
  ),
  identical(optimizer_fixture$audit$proposal_calls, 1L),
  isTRUE(all.equal(compile_result$best_score, 0.75)),
  identical(optimized$module_src, selected_fixture_source)
)

budget_summary
```

GEPA selected source is part of the compiled module. Render both complete
programs before using the result:

```{r router-source-review}
selected_source <- optimized$module_src

cat("Baseline source:\n", baseline$module_src, "\n\n")
cat("Selected source:\n", selected_source, "\n")

compile_result$lineage$best_candidate_id
compile_result$best_score
```

## Evaluate once on independent holdout data

These six tickets have different text from the training and validation rows.
The data object is created after `compile()`; the evaluations below happen
outside GEPA selection. The catalog knows three incident codes; the remaining
tickets use the task predictor.

```{r router-holdout}
holdout <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "[INC-DB-17] replicas unavailable",
    "[INC-SEC-9] login spray detected",
    "[INC-PAY-4] payment capture is delayed",
    "Reset email arrives after its token expires",
    "Duplicate charge after a plan upgrade",
    "Read traffic fails after failover"
  ),
  queue = c(
    "database",
    "security",
    "payments",
    "identity",
    "payments",
    "database"
  )
)

stopifnot(
  length(intersect(holdout$ticket, train$ticket)) == 0L,
  length(intersect(holdout$ticket, validation$ticket)) == 0L
)

compile_prompts <- optimizer_fixture$audit$prompts
holdout_absent_from_compile <- !any(vapply(
  holdout$ticket,
  grepl,
  logical(1),
  x = paste(compile_prompts, collapse = "\n"),
  fixed = TRUE
))
stopifnot(holdout_absent_from_compile)

accuracy <- metric_exact_match(field = "queue")
before_fixture <- new_route_fixture(model = "fixture-holdout-before")
after_fixture <- new_route_fixture(model = "fixture-holdout-after")

before <- evaluate(
  baseline,
  holdout,
  metric = accuracy,
  .llm = before_fixture$chat,
  .cache = FALSE,
  .progress = FALSE
)
after <- evaluate(
  optimized,
  holdout,
  metric = accuracy,
  .llm = after_fixture$chat,
  .cache = FALSE,
  .progress = FALSE
)

count_metadata_calls <- function(result, field) {
  sum(vapply(
    result$metadata,
    function(metadata) {
      value <- metadata[[field]]
      if (is.null(value)) 0L else as.integer(value)
    },
    integer(1)
  ))
}

heldout <- data.frame(
  program = c("baseline", "selected"),
  exact_match_quality = c(before$mean_score, after$mean_score),
  predictor_calls = c(
    count_metadata_calls(before, "predictor_calls"),
    count_metadata_calls(after, "predictor_calls")
  ),
  tool_calls = c(
    count_metadata_calls(before, "tool_calls"),
    count_metadata_calls(after, "tool_calls")
  ),
  fixture_model_calls = c(
    before_fixture$audit$task_calls,
    after_fixture$audit$task_calls
  )
)

heldout
```

The fixture counters and Flex trace metadata are execution counts. The
acceptance decision below uses the independent exact-match results and those
observed calls.

```{r router-acceptance}
same_quality <- isTRUE(before$mean_score == after$mean_score)
fewer_model_calls <- isTRUE(
  after_fixture$audit$task_calls < before_fixture$audit$task_calls
)
accepted <- same_quality && fewer_model_calls

decision <- data.frame(
  same_heldout_quality = same_quality,
  fewer_fixture_model_calls = fewer_model_calls,
  accepted = accepted
)
decision

stopifnot(
  isTRUE(before$mean_score == 1),
  isTRUE(after$mean_score == 1),
  isTRUE(heldout$predictor_calls[[1L]] == before_fixture$audit$task_calls),
  isTRUE(heldout$predictor_calls[[2L]] == after_fixture$audit$task_calls),
  isTRUE(heldout$predictor_calls[[1L]] == 6L),
  isTRUE(heldout$predictor_calls[[2L]] == 3L),
  isTRUE(heldout$tool_calls[[1L]] == 0L),
  isTRUE(heldout$tool_calls[[2L]] == 3L),
  isTRUE(accepted)
)
```

Here both programs route all six holdout tickets correctly. The selected
source uses three tool calls and three predictor calls; the baseline uses six
predictor calls. Treat this deterministic result as execution-path evidence;
a live search is needed to assess whether a model would invent the same
program.

`optimization_result()` keeps the compile budget and selection lineage
available for inspection:

```{r router-result}
list(
  best_candidate_id = compile_result$lineage$best_candidate_id,
  validation_score = compile_result$best_score,
  budget = budget_summary,
  holdout_absent_from_compile = holdout_absent_from_compile,
  heldout = heldout,
  acceptance = decision
)
```

## Try a live search

The deterministic journey above runs in documentation builds without
credentials. To try a stochastic search, install `mcptools` and its
`posit-mcp-repl` executable, then opt in to the chunk below. Optimizer-written
R should run with the default enforced-sandbox requirement.

```sh
Rscript -e 'install.packages("mcptools")'
uv tool install posit-mcp-repl
```

```{r live-gepa, eval=FALSE}
live_baseline <- flex(
  route_signature,
  module_src = baseline_source,
  tools = list(lookup_incident = lookup_incident),
  interpreter_factory = function() mcp_repl_runner(timeout = 45),
  source_format = "r",
  max_predictor_calls = 1L,
  max_tool_calls = 1L
)

task_chat <- ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-luna")
reflection_chat <- ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-astra")

live_optimized <- compile(
  live_baseline,
  GEPA(
    metric = route_metric,
    population_size = 4L,
    generations = 2L,
    selection = "current_best",
    seed = 42L,
    verbose = FALSE
  ),
  trainset = train,
  valset = validation,
  .llm = task_chat,
  .reflection_llm = reflection_chat,
  control = optimizer_control(
    max_metric_calls = 80L,
    max_provider_calls = 50L,
    max_cost = 1,
    progress = FALSE
  )
)

optimization_result(live_optimized)
```

Review the complete `module_src`, then evaluate the candidate once on a
holdout set that was not used for search. Keep the model, package version,
data splits, metric, seed and budget with the selected source.

## Choose the right source format

JSON is data describing an acyclic graph of `Predict` and
`ChainOfThought` steps. Its references point to outer inputs or earlier step
outputs, and Flex checks field types before execution. It needs no code
interpreter.

Executable R defines a top-level `forward()` function and can use
`Predict()`, `ChainOfThought()`, `Prediction()`, the other documented Flex
constructors, and the named tools you supplied. The source runs in a fresh
runner and crosses a versioned JSON bridge for predictor and tool calls. Host
tools retain their own permissions, even when the source runs in a sandbox.

`max_predictor_calls` and `max_tool_calls` bound the direct calls made by an
invocation. Agentic predictors such as ReAct or RLM have their own limits.
Guest-side computation runs again from the beginning after a bridged response,
so keep it pure and bound loops explicitly. Executable Flex runs dataset rows
sequentially and does not stream tokens.

Use Flex when the outcome is measurable and the best choice among model
calls, deterministic logic and selected tools is still open. If the workflow
is already clear, prefer a regular module or an explicit pipeline. See
[Choose an optimizer](advanced-optimization.html) for the other optimization
paths.

The article hides fixture setup from the main walkthrough. This chunk prints

run or adapt its response rules.

```{r offline-fixture-source, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat("```r\n")

}
